summary: Submitted a combined map update plus a first Candidate for the snapshot-store listing responsibility. The map (base version 3) adds B-snapshot-store-list (A6, producer of the new Fact F-snapshot-list-order) and makes B-snapshot-install consume that Fact, with a map_changes entry of impact=dependency for B-snapshot-install whose preserves text shows its id, Activity, owner, trigger, guards, sink-side writes and A1 cross-effect are unchanged, so Candidate 0e6f2e68d1704626a7ad26a172426d66 remains unaffected. The Candidate (action=continue) uses F-snapshot-list-order (lifecycle preservation) with the listing Behavior as direct producer and B-snapshot-install as the consumer/consequence, activity context A1/A6 where A1 is declared through B-snapshot-install's cross-activity effect and the consumer path. The sourced discrepancy: the SnapshotStore interface documents descending order with the highest index first (S-snapshot-list-contract) while FileSnapshotStore orders through sort.Reverse(snapMetaSlice) and snapMetaSlice.Less compares Term before Index (S-file-snapshot-list, S-file-snapshot-sort), so two retained snapshots with inversely ordered (term, index) put the lower-index snapshot first - the element sendLatestSnapshot opens to ship and the one NewRaft's restoreSnapshot tries to load. Counterevidence records that terms are non-decreasing with index within one log lineage, that only the in-repository store is bound by this comparator, that retention and filtering bound the participants, and that restore falls through to the next snapshot; the unknowns fix the discriminator (whether inversely ordered retained snapshots can coexist, whether the lower-index choice regresses applied state or breaks the startup scan, and whether term-first ordering is intentional). Preflight returned valid:true; the run's three earlier findings remain confirmed.
